$comment: GENERATED by scripts/gen_drops.py from spec/drops.v1.json — DO NOT EDIT. Handed to `claude -p --json-schema` by drops/plan.py.
title: DropPlan
description: A reading of one thing somebody shared into Builda, and the moves that could be made on it. Every move carries a VERBATIM span of the source text as its evidence; a move whose evidence is not found in the text is discarded before anybody sees it. Name nothing that is not in the text: no package that was not mentioned, no repository, no URL. When the text does not support a kind, answer `unknown` with a refusal code, which is a correct answer and not a failure.

kind.description: Exactly one. `unknown` is a real answer and is better than a kind that nearly fits.

title.description: What this is, in the reel's own terms. Not a description of the video. (max 80 chars)

summary.description: One sentence a builder could act on. No dashes. (max 200 chars)

confidence.description: 0-100: how sure the kind and the moves are, given how much text there actually was.

refusal.description: Set with kind `unknown` when there is nothing here to act on. Null when there is.

moves.description: Ordered, best first. Zero is correct for a refusal. Five is a ceiling, not a target. (max 5 items)

recipe.description: Only when kind is `recipe`, and only from what the reel actually said.

tags.description: Lowercase, one word or two, for filtering the board. Never a sentence. (each max 24 chars, max 6 items)

move_kind.description: What the runner would do. `keep` is a real move for something worth remembering and not worth doing.

title.description: The button's words, in the imperative: 'Install it', 'Add it to RideGT'. (max 80 chars)

intent.description: One sentence saying what done looks like. This becomes the runner's task, so it is specific. (max 200 chars)

evidence.description: VERBATIM from the caption or the transcript. A move whose evidence is not found there is dropped. (max 300 chars)

target.description: Where it happens. `existing_repo` means the person picks which one; the model never names a repository.

effort.description: How long it would take, at the coarsest useful grain. Three values, so nobody reads it as an estimate.

source.description: What to install and where it lives. Required in spirit for `install`, and the verifier enforces it.

serves.description: '4', 'two as a main'. Verbatim, and null when unsaid. (max 40 chars)

total_minutes.description: Only when stated. Never the sum of the steps: the reel's own claim or nothing.

ingredients.description: Every ingredient the reel named, in the order it named them. (1 to 40 items)

steps.description: The method, one step per entry. The step by step screen is one of these per card. (1 to 30 items)

equipment.description: Only what the reel showed or named. (each max 80 chars, max 8 items)

item.description: The ingredient, as the reel said it. (max 80 chars)

quantity.description: VERBATIM from the reel: '3 cloves', '1 1/2 cups'. Null when it never said one, which is not zero. (max 40 chars)

note.description: What is done to it before it goes in: 'minced', 'room temperature'. (max 40 chars)

text.description: One step, one thing to do, in the order it happens. (max 240 chars)

minutes.description: A timer, ONLY when the reel gave one. Null is 'it did not say', and the screen shows no timer.

source_kind.description: Where the thing lives. `docs_url` is the honest answer for a technique whose only home is a page.

ref.description: How the ecosystem names it: owner/repo, a package name, a formula. Never a sentence. (max 140 chars)

url.description: The one URL that is fetched before this move is shown. https only. (max 500 chars)
